name: genotype-01-control-panel
title: What do ParCa-level knockout mechanics look like across control gene classes?
claim: Knockout mechanics are structurally sound and class-independent (8/8 genotypes pass every fit-free integrity axis), but a step-3 dangling-reference crash in set_ppgpp_expression blocks the build for ALL ~393 ppGpp-regulated genes (~8% of the genome) - preempting any in-model essentiality signal - and the refit artifact for inert knockouts is per-mille in the bulk with ~10% shifts confined to the target's operon neighbors.
question: When genes of three verified classes are knocked out at the ParCa level - (A) expressed but functionally unwired in the model, (B) wired into metabolism but biologically non-essential, (C) essential machinery with three distinct mechanisms (RNA polymerase, ribosome, replisome) - what do the build mechanics actually do? Does every class build? Does the fit converge? How large is the expression perturbation beyond the deleted gene (the refit-artifact floor)? And is anything general or surprising in how the mechanics differ across classes?

assumptions.text: A ParCa build is deterministic given its inputs (WT rebuilds are byte-identical, measured 2026-08-13), so per-gene contrasts against one WT reference are attributable to the genotype + its refit, not to run-to-run noise.

A knockout that fails to build or fit is a RESULT, not an infrastructure failure. For essential machinery the fit may legitimately not converge; the runner records the failure mode (and retries with --allow-partial-fit to capture the partial state) rather than treating it as an error.

"Functionally unwired" is a claim about THIS model, not about biology. The same scan that classified this panel found tufA (EF-Tu), fusA (EF-G), infC (IF-3) and ftsZ are all expression-only - biologically lethal knockouts the model would read as inert. In-model essentiality can only live in explicitly wired machinery (RNAP, ribosomal proteins, replisome subunits, catalysts, TFs, two-component and equilibrium participants).

variants.name: ko-ygiB
variants.perturbation: Class A: ygiB (EG11164) - expressed, functionally unwired y-gene.
variants.expected_contrast: Builds clean; expression deltas at the refit-artifact floor; nothing else moves.

variants.name: ko-cspA
variants.perturbation: Class A: cspA (EG10166) - cold-shock protein, unwired, inert at 37C.
variants.expected_contrast: Same as ygiB - the second, higher-expression point on the floor.

variants.name: ko-pgi
variants.perturbation: Class B: pgi (EG10702) - glycolytic catalyst, biologically non-essential with a REAL growth defect.
variants.expected_contrast: Builds; the interesting question is whether the model registers any consequence at all - the expectation (Chris) is that it under-reacts relative to the real strain's growth defect.

variants.name: ko-tpiA
variants.perturbation: Class B: tpiA (EG11015) - triose-phosphate isomerase, same shape as pgi.

variants.name: ko-cheY
variants.perturbation: Class B/A bridge: cheY (EG10150) - biologically minor (chemotaxis), model-unwired.
variants.expected_contrast: Indistinguishable from class A - which is itself the datum.

variants.name: ko-rpoB
variants.perturbation: Class C: rpoB (EG10894) - RNAP core subunit. Transcription machinery.
variants.expected_contrast: Unknown - the point of the class. Candidate outcomes: build failure, fit non-convergence, or builds-with-nonsense. Whatever happens is recorded.

variants.name: ko-rplB
variants.perturbation: Class C: rplB (EG10865) - 50S ribosomal protein. Translation machinery.

variants.name: ko-dnaG
variants.perturbation: 'Class C: dnaG (EG10239) - primase, directly consumed as a replisome monomer subunit. Replication machinery.'
variants.expected_contrast: As rpoB, replication flavor - the most direct mechanistic dependency.

model_settings.name: run-mechanics
model_settings.detail: The parca composite is a 9-step DAG driven by its own CLI; runs go through canonical_runs (established on genotype-00, which also documents why the generic composite runner cannot drive this pipeline). All arms fast mode, and for these readouts that is provably lossless: a same-commit full-mode control (2026-08-18) found basal fit_cistron_expression BIT-IDENTICAL between --mode fast and --mode full (max relative difference 0.000 over 4,289 cistrons), and the KO refit artifact identical in both modes to four significant figures. Mechanistically expected - debug mode prunes the TF condition set (7 vs 51 cell_specs), which does not enter the basal expression fit. NOTE the same comparison run against the SHIPPED fixture shows ~3.6% differences; that fixture predates the #275 balance_translation_efficiencies fix, so those are code drift, not mode (fingerprint: 27 r-protein monomers, max delta 0.24). The control is therefore also a sensitivity check: the comparison detects real differences when they exist, and finds none between modes. ⚠ Scope: basal expression readouts. Fitted values that DO depend on the TF condition set are out of scope and unmeasured here. Measured cost, same hardware, cpus=8, as the SUM OF THE 9 PIPELINE STEPS (runtimes.json): full-mode WT 268.3 s, full-mode ygiB-KO 183.4 s; fast mode 81.6 s / 78.9 s. ⚠ Boundary: step sums exclude CLI startup, knowledge-base construction and the ~690 MB state write, so wall-clock is ~20 s larger - an earlier wall-clock reading of 288 s for the WT arm is consistent with this and is NOT what these figures measure. Either way the cost is minutes, not the "4-8 hours" the repo docs claim (docs are stale; see the lane notebook). Committed backing: data/evidence.json E-3, regenerated by sims/extract_evidence.py.

limitations: Fast regime throughout (7 of 51 conditions). Structural readouts are regime-independent; expression deltas are contrasts within one regime on one commit, so no fast-vs-full claim is needed or made here (a prior fast-vs-full comparison was confounded by fixture vintage - see the run-mechanics note); fitted-parameter VALUES are not read at all.

No graded biology bands, by design - this is mechanical characterization feeding the sms-ecoli investigations, not a phenotype claim. Findings name what was observed; anything alarming becomes an issue.
Single-gene knockouts only; class semantics are about the model's wiring, not biological essentiality (see the tufA/fusA/infC/ftsZ assumption).

every-panel-genotype-produces-a-recorded.detail: 8/8 genes have bundle + card verdict + a recorded ParCa outcome in data/panel_summary.json; the four build failures are recorded with their failure tails and --allow-partial-fit retry results (also failed - the crash precedes the fit).

structural-integrity-holds-for-every-gen.detail: 8/8 genotypes (including the four whose ParCa later crashes) grade within_tol on every fit-free structural axis - the genome surgery is correct for every gene class; the crashes are downstream of a structurally sound knowledge base.

findings.statement: In-model essentiality can only live in explicitly wired machinery: the classification scan for this panel found tufA (EF-Tu), fusA (EF-G), infC (IF-3), and ftsZ are expression-only - no functional wiring in complexation, metabolism, regulation, two-component, equilibrium, or any functional molecule group - so knocking out these biologically essential genes would read as inert. Conversely dnaG, which a complexation-only scan misses, is directly consumed as a replisome monomer subunit.

evidence.observed: Participation scan over the full-condition fixture sim_data, 2026-08-17: 3,386 functionally referenced species after excluding the bulk_molecules_binomial_division inventory (16,321 entries - every bulk molecule, which had masked all distinctions).

findings.next_action: Holds interpretation weight for every KO study: absence of model response to a KO must be checked against wiring before being read as a model prediction.

findings.statement: The knockout mechanics are uniform and structurally sound across every gene class: all 8 genotypes generate bundles, and all 8 grade within_tol on every fit-free structural axis (round trip, chromosome length, bounds, tombstone, functional absence) - including the four whose ParCa fit later crashes. The genome-surgery layer is class-independent.

A ParCa-level knockout of ANY ppGpp-regulated gene crashes the build at step 3: set_ppgpp_expression (transcription.py:1935) indexes its fold-change table by cistron id, the deleted gene's cistron has left the functional index, and the lookup raises KeyError('<gene>_RNA'). 393 genes (~8% of the genome) are in ppgpp_regulated_genes, so this is the blast radius. The class-C "essentiality" signal is entirely preempted by this crash - cspA (class A: functionally unwired, biologically dispensable at 37C) fails identically to rpoB/rplB/dnaG, proving the failure is regulon membership, not essentiality. This is the first FATAL instance of the D17 dangling-reference class (the generator prunes nothing by design; consequences are this investigation's subject matter), and what "essential machinery" would do in the model remains unobserved.

evidence.observed: Identical failure tails for cspA, rpoB, rplB, dnaG (KeyError on EG10166_RNA / EG10894_RNA / EG10865_RNA / EG10239_RNA respectively); --allow-partial-fit does not help (the crash precedes the fit). len(ppgpp_regulated_genes) = 393 (8.7% of the 4538 functional cistrons; 4747 raw genes would give 8.3% - the cistron set is the one set_ppgpp_expression indexes, so it is the operative denominator). Crash-vs-regulon-membership agrees 8/8 with ZERO mismatches across the panel. Committed backing: data/evidence.json E-1, regenerated by sims/extract_evidence.py.

findings.next_action: FILED as v2ecoli#536 (composition defect: KO generator x set_ppgpp_expression - same family as v2ecoli#490's DnaA-box drop, but fatal rather than silent). Scoped there: the sibling TF fold-change loader (simulation_data.py:146-190) already carries the coordinate guard this site lacks, so a TF knockout does NOT crash - it drops the affected fold-change entries silently instead, behind VERBOSE=False. One-site fix, not a sweep. Candidate fixes belong to the consumer per the D17/#468 precedent: skip or renormalize fold-change entries whose cistron left the functional set. Until fixed, panel and screen gene lists must exclude ppgpp_regulated_genes or expect a build failure - which the runner already records as a result.

findings.statement: The refit artifact for a functionally-inert knockout has a clean three-part structure: (a) a per-mille bulk shift (median relative expression delta 0.02-0.16% across the four builders, scaling with the deleted gene's freed expression share), (b) ~10-12% shifts confined to the deleted gene's OPERON NEIGHBORS (ygiB's tail is ygiC and tolC - transcription-unit share reattribution after TU truncation), and (c) large relative deltas on numerically-zero cistrons (1e-24-scale expression) that mean nothing. The wired-but-nonessential class (pgi, tpiA - genes with real growth defects) is barely distinguishable from a chemotaxis gene at the expression level, consistent with the expectation that the model under-reacts to their loss.

evidence.observed: expression_delta_vs_wt in data/panel_summary.json: ygiB median 2.1e-4 / pgi 9.2e-4 / tpiA 1.6e-3 / cheY 8.2e-4; >5% tails 0.1-0.3% of cistrons; ygiB's >5% tail is 9 cistrons, of which exactly 2 carry real expression: ygiC (EG11165_RNA) and tolC (EG11009_RNA), both at 12.35%; the other 7 sit below a 1e-12 zero floor and their relative deltas are meaningless. Committed backing: data/evidence.json E-2, regenerated by sims/extract_evidence.py.

findings.next_action: Directly actionable for the Ambr250 comparison's DEG grading: mask the target's operon neighbors and near-zero cistrons, and treat the per-mille bulk as the artifact floor. Growth-rate-level under-reaction (pgi/tpiA) is a simulation-layer question, out of scope for a ParCa-only panel. Scope, now measured rather than argued (2026-08-18): the magnitudes are MODE-INDEPENDENT. A same-commit full-mode WT/ygiB-KO control reproduces this contrast to full float precision, not merely to four significant figures: median relative delta 2.1025575e-04 and >5% tail 0.210% are IDENTICAL in fast and full, the named tail is ygiC/tolC at 12.35% in both, and full-vs-fast basal WT expression is bit-identical (max relative delta exactly 0.0). So both the structure (TU-neighbor concentration, mechanism-derived) and the numbers carry over; consumers may use them directly. Committed backing: data/evidence.json E-3.
